label.title: Rights, Freedoms, and Governmental Legitimacy

claims.claim_text: Commitment to continue to honor treaty and trust obligations and respect cultural rights.
Support for self-determination for all oppressed people.
Commitment to consistently act in accord with the greatest values of the country – freedom and opportunity for all.
Commitment to advance the ability of all persons to live with dignity, security, and respect, regardless of who they are or who they love.
Commitment to return the Nation to its best traditions, including a commitment to government by law.
Commitment to redress the systemic injustices that have long plagued society.
Support for restoring the ethic of public service through service in the military, reserve forces, or diplomatic corps that keep the nation free and safe.
Commitment to continue to honor both religious freedom and other civil rights, not put them at war with one another.
Commitment to continue to press for human rights, the rule of law, and political freedom.
Affirmation of the inherent dignity and worth of all people.
The only just government is one that governs with the consent of the governed.
Government does not confer rights to life, liberty, and property, but is instituted by men to protect the rights that man already possesses.

prompt:

facts or infer positions for groups absent from the examples. If the claims mainly
concern political actors, campaign narratives, or organizing rather than a coherent
policy subject, say so plainly in both title and caveat. Party names can appear
only when the party itself is the subject. Avoid vague titles like 'Policy and Society'.

{"title": "specific subject, at most 9 words",

The keywords are retrieval aids, not additional factual evidence.
